newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland says Lukashenko breaks constitutional rules.
newsitem.headline: Poland says Lukashenko breaks constitutional rules.

text.p: Poland's foreign minister said on Thursday Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko had clearly violated constitutional principles and that Warsaw wanted to avert undemocratic developments in the neighbouring state.
The speaker of Poland's parliament meanwhile announced that a delegation of deputies from all parties would leave for Belarus on Friday.

"We have already expressed our great unease at the development on events in Belarus. There has been a clear violation of constitutional rules by President Lukashenko," Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati told a news conference.

Rosati recalled that Poland, whose border with Belarus is almost 300 km (200 miles) long, had already expressed concern and its President Aleksander Kwasniewski had issued a joint statement with his Ukrainian and Lithuanian counterparts.

"Everything is aimed, in our intentions, towards preventing unconstitutional solutions which would infringe democratic principles and human rights in that country," he said. Poland had important interests in Belarus and wanted to maintain good relations.
Rosati's comments went further than previous Polish comments on Belarus, where Lukashenko is clashing with parliament over his plan to hold a referendum on Sunday on extending his powers.
The speaker of the Polish parliament said the all-party delegation would be led by deputy speaker Olga Krzyzanowska.

The spokesman for the opposition Union for Freedom party told Reuters the delegation aimed to demonstrate international concern and solidarity with Belarus parliamentarians and might offer to mediate in the dispute if both sides were willing.

Kwasniewski, Lithuania's Algirdas Brazauskas and Ukraine's Leonid Kuczma issued a statement on Wednesday calling for a constitutional resolution of the conflict -- a ground-breaking joint initiative by the three states bordering on Belarus.

Rosati said Poland, which was consulting with Western and Russian ministries, as well as the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe which was offering to mediate in Belarus, had won praise from the West for its actions.
"It is accepted that Poland has become an initiator or leader in a regional approach to the question of Belarus, and these initiatives have been very highly assessed," he said.

Poland, a front-runner for North Atlantic Treaty Organisation membership, sees one of its tasks in this process as cultivating good relations with its eastern neighbours, partly to avoid entrenching new divisions across Europe.
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin arrived in Minsk on Thursday to try to resolve the crisis there, Itar-Tass news agency reported.
